correctness.rationale: On the closed simplex the escort map is bijective, with inverse p_i=y_i^(1/q)/Z, and D_q=Z^(q/(q-1)). The affine escort slice is compact; minimizing the strictly convex power sum for q<1 or maximizing the strictly concave one for q>1 gives uniqueness. For q>=1 a move toward a strictly positive feasible vector improves any boundary candidate at an interior budget, by the singular power or Shannon derivative at zero. For q<1, parameterize y=(1-b+t,b-2t,t) with max(0,b-1)<=t<=b/2. At the upper endpoint the derivative divided by 1/q is (1-b/2)^s+(b/2)^s>0, ruling out absence of the middle species. For b<=1 the sign at t=0 is that of (1-b)^s-2b^s, giving the exact threshold, including equality by strict convexity. Reflection covers b>=1; at b=1 the lower endpoint derivative is negative, and b=0,2 force singletons. Near the transition the unique minimizer has t->0. Subtracting the derivative at t=0 before Taylor expansion gives K delta(1+o(1))=t^s+(L+o(1))t, making each of the three balances rigorous. Inverting the escort gives the stated A_q and exponent; at q=1/2 the coefficient is 9/20, also obtained from the exact interior t=delta/2 and Z_0=5/9.
residual_risks: The onset is one-sided for fixed q; it is not uniform at q=0, q=1 or across q=1/2. The finite scripted checks do not establish the continuous-parameter result.

value.rationale: Three equally spaced capacities give the first nontrivial escort slice with an adjustable support. A generic truncated stationary form says an abundance may vanish but does not quantify its sensitivity to the budget. The exact onset and its crossover distinguish two different scaling mechanisms and give a sharp benchmark for users of this model. This is mathematical benchmark sensitivity, not a biological extinction prediction.
residual_risks: Scope is the equality-constrained, equally spaced three-capacity benchmark. No extrapolation to uneven scores or population dynamics was assessed.
